title: What is KOL marketing? A practical guide for medtech teams
overview: What is KOL marketing? How medtech and medical device companies work with key opinion leaders to create content physicians trust, from KOL video to peer-to-peer education.
author: Made Clear
body:
What is KOL marketing? In medtech, it means working with key opinion leaders (KOLs), the physicians whose research, teaching and clinical results shape how their peers practise, to explain a therapy or device to the people who will use it. Done well, it isn't endorsement. It's education delivered by the people the audience already trusts.

Interventional cardiologists, radiologists and surgeons are trained to question claims. A brochure or a sales slide from a manufacturer starts on the back foot. The same evidence explained by a respected operator, in their own words and with their own cases, is heard very differently. That difference is the whole point of key opinion leader marketing.

Why key opinion leader marketing works in medtech

Credibility. A KOL has stood where the audience stands: in the cath lab, with a difficult lesion and a decision to make. When they describe how a device performs, physicians listen as peers, not as targets.

Clinical depth. KOLs can walk through a real patient case, the imaging and the outcome. That level of detail is what changes clinical behaviour, and it's very hard for a marketing team to deliver on its own.

Reach. Leading physicians teach, lecture and publish. Content made with them travels through their networks, societies and congress programmes as well as your own channels.

What KOL content looks like

KOL content covers a wide range of formats. The most useful ones we make include:

  • KOL video interviews: short, focused films on a single question, such as patient selection, technique or what the latest data means.
  • Case presentations: a KOL walks through a real case, from the angiogram to the result.
  • Documentary series: longer films that tell the story of a therapy through the people who have used it.
  • Peer-to-peer education programmes: structured courses taught by a faculty of KOLs.
  • Congress content: interviews, booth presentations and social clips captured while KOLs are gathered in one place.
  • Immersive experiences: VR and interactive formats presented by KOLs.

For The Calcium Masterclass, we produced a 10-part, TV-series style programme with Shockwave Medical and Optima Education, taught by a world-class faculty from Europe and the US. It attracted over 5,500 cardiologists, who spent an average of 28 minutes each learning about the procedure. For The Curious Case of Coronary Calcium, two leading interventional cardiologists present a real patient case inside a 25-minute VR experience.

KOL engagement: making it a partnership

Good KOL engagement starts long before the camera rolls. The physicians you work with are busy and protective of their reputation. They will commit to content that is scientifically sound, respects their time and gives them something worth saying.

  • Involve them early. Let KOLs shape the story and choose the cases. On Big Discrepancies, Big Solutions, iVascular's KOL selected the case that best showed how the Angiolite stent performs across vessel sizes, then described the procedure in a studio interview.
  • Keep it educational. Content that feels like an advert puts both the KOL and the audience off. Lead with the clinical question.
  • Plan around their diaries. Congresses are the easiest time to film several KOLs at once. We cover this in how to make the most of your KOLs at congresses worldwide.
  • Make it easy to say yes. Clear briefs, agreed questions, a crew that knows the science and a short, well-run shoot.

Where KOL marketing goes wrong

The most common problems are avoidable:

  • One KOL used for everything, so the message starts to feel scripted.
  • Footage shot with no plan for how it will be used, so it sits on a drive.
  • Content written for marketing, not for physicians, so the KOL won't share it.
  • No distribution plan. A strong KOL video only works if the right people see it.

Measuring KOL marketing

Track what physicians actually do with the content, not just how many people it reached. Watch time, completion, enquiries from the field team and the questions physicians ask at the next congress all tell you more than impressions. For Medtronic's HTN:RDN programme, a four-part documentary and a sustained expert-led programme reached 4 million healthcare professionals, drove 117k content views and a fivefold increase in searches for renal denervation.

Getting started

Start with the clinical question your audience is asking, then find the KOLs best placed to answer it. Decide which formats you need and where they will be seen, and plan the filming around when those KOLs are available. If you'd like help, see our KOL content work or get in touch.
